Ledger

Every published record and the gates it passed.

Two different kinds of record appear on every card below:

Text relation

A claim about what Jung wrote, gated against the paragraph it cites. The quote is checked mechanically, then a model of a different family reads the full paragraph and judges whether it supports the claim, in the right direction, in the right voice. This is the verification the project's method claim is about.

Family assignment

A classification of a relation that is already verified: which kind of relation it is, drawn from a fixed vocabulary. Two model arms classify blind, a calibrated gate checks them, and a human rules where they disagree. It says nothing new about the text and never re-opens the gate above it.

Each reference shows its full verification trail: the deterministic quote check, the independent gate (verifier and date), the narrow voice audit, the cross-vendor check, and, where a person has checked the paragraph, human validation from the gold set. Disputed records link to the dispute log.

653 nodes · 2420 edges · 3180 references · 100% gate-verified · 2986 cross-vendor checked · 50 human-validated · 18 disputes on record · 1906 family-assigned · 428 awaiting a ruling · 86 unclassified · full commit history

The text filter is the broadest control here and the rows under it narrow further: chips in one row combine with OR, rows combine with AND, and the filter applies to whatever they leave. The counts beside a chip are graph-wide and do not change as you filter, so a filtered view can never read as a total. A volume count is records citing that volume, so a record with references in two volumes is counted under both. Every card carries a § permalink.
